predecessors.name: Joseon
predecessors.text: all of Joseon: the Korean Empire was 'proclaimed in October 1897 by King Gojong of the Joseon dynasty'; infobox predecessor Joseon

successors.name: Japan (Empire of Japan, 1868-1947)
successors.text: the whole of Korea: 'complete and permanent cession to His Majesty the Emperor of Japan of all rights of sovereignty over the whole of Korea' (Article 1)

ledger.x: 1897: King Gojong proclaims the Korean Empire and is crowned emperor at Hwangudan.
1901: Korea sends police into Jiandao, the Tumen's north bank.
1904: Japanese troops land at Incheon and occupy Hanseong, then the rest of Korea.
1905: the wartime occupation becomes the protectorate.
1909: the Gando Convention leaves Jiandao to China.

wars.name: Russo-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Japanese victory; the Treaty of Portsmouth (5 September 1905) 'recognized Japanese interests in Korea'; Korea, which had pursued a policy of neutrality, became a Japanese protectorate on 17 November 1905.

wars.name: Jiandao (Gando) border dispute
wars.outcome: Korean police entered Jiandao in 1901 and stayed to 1906; Japan 'invaded Jiandao in August 1907' as Korea's protector and in the 1909 Gando Convention 'affirmed territorial rights of the Qing over Jiandao'.
